newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Bulgarian president says IMF cash vital for reform.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian president says IMF cash vital for reform.

text.p: Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov said on Friday a loan agreement with the IMF was vital if economic reform was to succeed in his country.

Stoyanov, speaking during a visit to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty headquarters in Prague, said Sofia hoped to win a new loan from the International Monetary Fund before April's parliamentary election.

"I do not want my country to be seen as a beggar. We need this financial assistance because otherwise this upsurge, this public aspiration for reform and transatlantic integration may be nipped in the bud because of the extremely low standards of living," he said.
An IMF mission is in Bulgaria to discuss a new standby agreement to help the country stabilise its crumbling economy and repay foreign debts.
"We are hoping to get this loan from the IMF even before the election," Stoyanov said, speaking through an interpreter.
He did not mention how much IMF money Bulgaria was hoping to receive.

The president, on an official visit to the Czech Republic, said Bulgaria was in a severe economic crisis but added, "Public sentiment has never been so clearly and categorically in favour of rapid economic reform and European integration."
Stoyanov mediated a deal in early February providing for early elections on April 19, dissolved parliament and appointed a caretaker cabinet.
The cabinet has, among other pledges, promised to speed up privatisation and close loss-making state firms.
It has also adopted a declaration, stating its desire to be a full member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).
The handling of the economy by the previous Socialist government threw Bulgaria into chaos, prompting 30 days of widespread strikes and political squabbling.
Stoyanov said the caretaker government had to act quickly and take reform to the point of no returm.
"We have wasted a lot of time. We have made a mistake and we have no right to repeat it," he said.
Asked to predict the election result, Stoyanov said:
"What I expect from the coming election is a strong parliamentary majority with a matching executive which will carry on with the reforms just started and lead them to a successful conclusion."
